utterances.text: So would I be correct in saying that every time you drink heavily, you are unable to eat?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I would spend three or four days without eating. I mean, I wouldn't have a single bite of anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, you told us on Tuesday that in order to get out of it, not only do you need an infusion, but you need some assistance in eating again; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I receive treatment, vitamins, Beviplex, in particular, which was supposed to boost my appetite. I was also given medication to calm down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I now want to ask you about your work in the Territorial Defence. Is it correct that you began to work with the Territorial Defence after the 19th of May, when a mobilisation order was issued from the local Serb Territorial Defence of Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was on the 19th of May that we were mobilised. I was in the village of Prelovo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, from the time that you were mobilised on the 19th of May until the day that you say you went into the hospital, you no longer worked as a waiter; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether that means it's not correct or whether he didn't work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you clarify that? Does that mean that you no longer worked as a waiter?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I no longer worked as a waiter. Just to make ourselves clear, if you're referring to the entire period of time -- no, you said until the 14th of June. From the 19th of May until the 14th of June, when I broke my leg, no, I was not working as a waiter during that period of time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Panos restaurant remain open during that period?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The only thing that still worked was the section next to the Panos restaurant, and it was called Grill. It only belonged to our establishment. But the restaurant itself did not work. Panos was closed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the 19th of May, you reported to the TO, or Territorial Defence, command in Prelovo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the last time that you worked for the TO in Prelovo was the 28th or 29th of May; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that time period, were you given any days off?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I was, because it was the very beginning. There was a lot of work. The kitchen needed to be fully equipped. I don't think I was given any day off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your testimony was -- do you recall whether it was the 28th or the 29th?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think I was in detention for three or maybe four days. I'm not sure. The 28th, 29th, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you went into detention because on your last day, either the 28th or 29th, you refused to carry the night-time meal, the night-time meal, because you were afraid; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I always tried not to have to carry that night-time meal. But the chief reason was that the front line had been moved for another five kilometres which meant that I would have to carry it another five kilometres to supply that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the last meal that you participated in the preparation or delivery of was the lunchtime meal on the 28th or the 29th; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your service with the Territorial Defence in Prelovo was a total of either nine and a half or ten and a half days; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, incidentally, when the front line moved, it moved to the village of Rujiste; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the village of Rujiste is the place where the Lukic family lives; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is. There are also the Lipovac family, Ivanovic family; Kadic is another family living there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you friends with some of these other families that you are now telling us about?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I did know them, but that was very far away from me. It's a village. Besides, they don't all live there. A number of them work abroad; a number of them were in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of the families, particularly the Lukic family, have to evacuate the village because of the fighting around the village?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean by "evacuate it."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of the people have to leave their homes because it was not safe for them to remain in the village so close to the front line?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that Dragan and Milan Lukic left. Milan Lukic, that's an elderly man, and his brother. I learned that when I was on the front line in 1993. They took their livestock and all and went to Serbia, and I think spent about a year there. I'm not sure how long. Two brothers, elderly men, both of them, Milan and Dragan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were their homes in Rujiste destroyed as a result of the fighting?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: By Muslims, you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By either side.

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, none of the houses had burnt down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any of the Lukic family hurt in this fighting in their village?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milan Lukic was killed in 1993, I believe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you now to tell us about the time when you were in Prelovo, from the 19th of May until the 28th or 29th of May. During that period of time, was anybody hurt from this village that you are aware of?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that. I don't know. No, I'm not aware.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you were mobilised, you received a specific instruction to go to the quartermaster in the Prelovo command; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your responsibility in the Territorial Defence was to assist in the transportation of food from the town of Visegrad up to Prelovo, where it was then distributed to the soldiers on the front line; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not food -- meals were prepared there. So what we carried over there were foodstuffs; that is, we would purchase that in Visegrad and then carry the foodstuffs. And the kitchen itself was in Prelovo, so that's where the meals were prepared, where the food was prepared.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you were involved in both aspects of that job. Isn't it true that you were involved in transporting the foodstuffs from Visegrad to Prelovo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And isn't it also true that you were also involved in the preparation and distribution of that food after it was cooked in Prelovo?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I would transport it further on. There was a cook who took care of that, again an elderly man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You yourself were not engaged in any combat activities on the front line, were you?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't. That was not my duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At some point, or I should say on the 28th or the 29th, you are arrested and you are placed in the Uzamnica barracks that was being used as a detention centre; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us on Tuesday that during your work in Prelovo, you continued to drink; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would I be correct in saying that you continued to drink quite heavily?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time of the day would you typically begin to drink when you were working in Prelovo?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never stopped.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So would you drink or take a drink as soon as you woke up in the morning?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what I usually did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you remained in Uzamnica barracks until you were released to attend the funeral of your cousin; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was released when he was killed, after he was killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Domazet has introduced two documents into evidence today, and from those documents we know that your cousin was killed on the 1st of June and buried on the 6th of June. Does that agree with your recollection of his death?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was released on the 1st, when he got killed, and I know that they couldn't pull him out straight away. Now, how many days then passed by, I wouldn't know, because he was killed in the woods so it took time to find him, to get him out. And I attended the funeral.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you're certain that it was on the day that he was killed that you were released; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the entire time that you were imprisoned, you were on a hunger strike?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why did you go on a hunger strike?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I had been detained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was the last time on either the 28th or the 29th that you took food?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, dear, I don't know. How can I know any such thing?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you refuse all of your meals in Uzamnica?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not the first day, because I thought they'd let me go, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So either on the 29th or the 30th of June, you ate the food that was offered you in Uzamnica?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Have you got the right month there? We're talking about May, aren't we?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I apologise. Yes, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So either on the 29th or 30th of May, you ate the food that was offered to you in Uzamnica?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I guess that was the case. All I know is that I did go on strike.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you didn't -- once you stopped eating, you did not eat again until you were released from gaol?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. Dr. Vasiljevic came to give -- to administer an infusion. Now, whether he came that day or the day before my cousin was killed, but it was then that I was given infusion. Now, I wouldn't know the -- exactly, I wouldn't be able to give you the exact date. All I know is that when they told me he had been killed, they let me go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why was it that you were given an infusion?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that doctor is a relative and he knows, he knew about my drinking problem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Using your manner of describing your own drinking habits, how deep were you into your alcohol addiction on the day you were arrested?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I could always have a drink, and I kept it well, I remained on my feet regardless. So what do I know?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I know that you do not drive, but would you have considered yourself too drunk to get behind the wheel of a car or operate machinery? Would you have been too drunk for that?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd be too afraid to drive. I'd be just too afraid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because of the amount of alcohol that you were consuming at that time?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't think I'd be able to drive a car. I really don't know how to tell you. I mean, your reflexes are not all that good when you drink. But besides, I never -- I never had a driving license, so I really don't know how it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your mind, did your drinking affect your ability to do your job in Prelovo properly?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, naturally. I know when I work my regular job as a waiter, I know what a huge difference it is. Whenever -- I mean, whatever kind of work might be at issue. Even when you sleep there is a difference.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that your incarceration in Uzamnica is also consistent with your superiors deciding that you should be punished for being drunk at work?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think, yes, that was their chief reasoning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So their reason for putting you into gaol had more to do with you being drunk on duty than your refusal to go to deliver food at night; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't really know what they thought. Perhaps they thought that I would sober up and -- no, you know, when I drink and then I stop, then I just don't drink for another three or four months. And then if I start drinking again, then -- when I start drinking, then it's hard for me to pull away. Very seldom it was that I, for instance, would get drunk and then stop the next day. Yes, it did happen now and then, but not very often.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet has provided the Prosecution with some of the statements of some of the Defence witnesses that will come in a few weeks to testify. Have you had an opportunity to see those statements?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Dr. Goran Loncarevic's, Alexander Moljevic's. Are you referring to the medical people or all the statements?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm just asking you, have you seen the statements generally? Have you had an opportunity to read them?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you realise that one of those witnesses will take the witness chair and intends to tell us that the reason you were placed in gaol was because you were drunk? Is that person mistaken or is that person correct?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he is right. Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, would you also agree with me that what you're calling a hunger strike, refusing to eat for two or possibly three days, that that is equally consistent with something that happens to you quite frequently when you drink alcohol?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. I wouldn't have been able to eat much anyway, especially those first days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So let me ask you again, was your not eating as a result of your addiction to alcohol or was it the result of your decision to go on a hunger strike?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not want to eat, and what -- I mean, who knows at such a time? And I wouldn't have been able to eat much. I could never eat when I drank. Even if I did eat, that would be very little.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us about the Uzamnica gaol? Was it crowded?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was only one other man with me, Pero Simcic, and he too was arrested when drunk.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was his ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there Muslims present in the gaol?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were not with us. If there were any, they were not with us. We were in a separate room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of Muslims being detained in another part or another room of the gaol?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were some. I don't know how many. But we were kept separately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did you become aware of Muslims in the gaol? Could you hear them, or were you told that they were there?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was said, but I just don't know what to tell you. I don't know how many and why they were there, because we did not have any contact with them. As a matter of fact, this Simcic, he spent there only a day, or maybe two, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So just to summarise what you were doing between the 19th of May and the 14th of June, when you say you went into the hospital, from the 19th to the 28th or the 29th, you worked in Prelovo until you were arrested; that's correct?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from the 1st to the 14th, you were not incarcerated, and you were in the town of Visegrad; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've already told us that you yourself never fought on the battlefield with the TO. My question to you is did you ever tell anyone that you fought with the TO on the battlefield?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was on the front in 1995, not on the front, on the front line, not on the battlefield. But that I participated in taking the front lines, no, I did not do that. How shall I put it? When front lines are attacked, no, I didn't do that. But I was in sheds, I stood guard, and things of that sort.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what is different between "front line" and "battlefield"? Can you describe the difference?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when you establish a front line, for instance, we hold it Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. on one side, and then a kilometre or two away, perhaps more, perhaps less, is where the Muslims hold their front line. And then you make a shed or something. You have a stove; you can make a fire. But nobody ever touched anyone. They left us alone, we left them alone, and that was that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the battlefield would be the area between the two front lines; would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, now, if -- just in case they attacked us or if we attacked them, then, yes, that would be it. But it just didn't happen, that, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to ask my question again to you and I want you to just focus on the period of 1992. Did you ever tell anyone that in 1992 you had fought with the TO on the battlefield?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was never on the battlefield.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to ask you a few specific questions about your work in Prelovo. How many trips would you make between Visegrad and Prelovo each day?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: At least one; at times, two, if I needed to bring something more for the kitchen. But once -- there would be one trip a day to get the foodstuffs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what vehicle would you use?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had a van.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that an official Territorial Defence van?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the van which belonged to Sumarstvo, to the forestry company, which had been requisitioned for the Territorial Defence, so that the driver who worked for the company also drove that vehicle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on the nights that you would stay in your own home, would you get a ride up to Prelovo in this van?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You mean when I went home, from Prelovo to my home?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you about from Visegrad to Prelovo. Would the van pick up the foodstuffs in Visegrad, collect you, and then go up to Prelovo for the day's work?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I had to go. I had to go there to get these foodstuffs, being the quartermaster.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had to go to Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you meet the van in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: Mitar Vasiljevic [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It would stop by my house, because my house is before Visegrad, and pick me up.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, do you want me to break there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. We will resume at 9.30 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 26th day of October, 2001, at 9.30 a.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
